perspective:
From Arthur Chung’s accessible perspective:

- He knows he is Arthur Chung, a doctorate-holding plumber, and that he collaborates with Teresa Ortega, a medical assistant colleague, on community service projects.
- He observed Teresa working hard and appearing overwhelmed. He offered help. Teresa said she could manage but had a lot to do. He insisted, mentioning self-care and working faster together. Teresa accepted help organizing medical supplies, and they began.
- He believed Teresa was hesitant to accept help because she wanted to prove her capability. He told her he admired her self-reliance and that accepting help did not mean she was incapable. Teresa said she wanted to show she could do it by herself. He reassured her about teamwork and support. Teresa agreed she sometimes needs reminding.
- He believed Teresa was still struggling and felt frustrated that his help was not producing results. He told her he could see things were still tough and that she was doing a great job. Teresa said it had been busy and she felt behind. He proposed working together instead of just helping. Teresa agreed, and they decided to tackle tasks as a team.
- He felt hopeful about the collaborative approach. Teresa said it already felt less overwhelming. He suggested handling inventory while she managed patient records, with regular check-ins. Teresa agreed and was glad. He was glad and wanted a productive day.
- He believed their teamwork paid off and they accomplished more together. Teresa agreed it was a great experience. He suggested continuing collaboration on future projects. Teresa agreed they were more efficient and effective as a team. He said he looked forward to their next project; Teresa thanked him for being supportive.

He does not have access to Teresa’s private thoughts, only her statements and his own observations/inferences.
